WILDFIRE SMOKE PROTECTION — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Alex Lee · Acme Corp

ABOUT THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This Wildfire Smoke Protection — Information Sheet describes California's Cal/OSHA wildfire smoke standard, 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1, which addresses employee exposure to wildfire smoke in the workplace. It covers when the standard applies, what workplaces and situations are exempt, the employer's duties to identify smoke hazards and communicate them to employees, training requirements, and the engineering, administrative, and respirator control measures required as air quality worsens. It states information about this regulation; it does not evaluate the air quality at any particular worksite or determine whether a particular employer has complied with the standard on any given day.

Employer: Acme Corp
Employee: Jordan Alex Lee
Program contact: Taylor Morgan

WHEN THE STANDARD APPLIES
The wildfire smoke standard applies to a workplace only when two conditions are both met. First, an air-quality condition: 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1(a)(1)(A) provides that the standard applies where "[t]he current Air Quality Index (current AQI) for PM2.5 is 151 or greater, regardless of the AQI for other pollutants." An AQI of 151 or greater for PM2.5 corresponds to the "Unhealthy" category or worse on the regulation's own six-category table (Good, Moderate, Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups, Unhealthy, Very Unhealthy, and Hazardous). Second, a foreseeability condition: subsection (a)(1)(B) requires that "[t]he employer should reasonably anticipate that employees may be exposed to wildfire smoke." Both conditions must be present for the standard to apply to a given workplace at a given time.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "The current Air Quality Index (current AQI) for PM2.5 is 151 or greater, regardless of the AQI for other pollutants; and"
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (a)(1)(A) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  "The employer should reasonably anticipate that employees may be exposed to wildfire smoke."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (a)(1)(B) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  Known gap: This clause states the two applicability conditions in the regulation's own text. It does not address how "should reasonably anticipate" has been applied to any particular set of facts, and no case law construing that phrase was independently verified for this document.

EXEMPT WORKPLACES AND SITUATIONS
8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1(a)(2) exempts several categories of workplaces and operations from the standard even when the AQI threshold in subsection (a)(1) is met. Filtered enclosed spaces are exempt: the regulation exempts "[e]nclosed buildings or structures in which the air is filtered by a mechanical ventilation system and the employer ensures that windows, doors, bays, and other openings are kept closed, except when it is necessary to open doors to enter or exit," and separately exempts "[e]nclosed vehicles in which the air is filtered by a cabin air filter and the employer ensures that windows, doors, and other openings are kept closed, except when it is necessary to open doors to enter or exit the vehicle." Brief exposure is also exempt: the regulation exempts "[e]mployees exposed to a current AQI for PM2.5 of 151 or greater for a total of one hour or less during a shift." A specific occupational exemption applies to "[f]irefighters engaged in wildland firefighting." A further exemption applies where the employer independently measures PM2.5 at the worksite in accordance with the regulation's Appendix A and demonstrates the concentration does not correspond to an AQI of 151 or greater.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "Enclosed buildings or structures in which the air is filtered by a mechanical ventilation system and the employer ensures that windows, doors, bays, and other openings are kept closed, except when it is necessary to open doors to enter or exit."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (a)(2)(A) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  "Enclosed vehicles in which the air is filtered by a cabin air filter and the employer ensures that windows, doors, and other openings are kept closed, except when it is necessary to open doors to enter or exit the vehicle."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (a)(2)(B) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  "Employees exposed to a current AQI for PM2.5 of 151 or greater for a total of one hour or less during a shift."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (a)(2)(D) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  "Firefighters engaged in wildland firefighting."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (a)(2)(E) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  Known gap: This clause does not restate the technical PM2.5-measurement methodology in the regulation's Appendix A, which was not independently fetched or verified for this document.

KEY TERMS: AQI, PM2.5, AND WILDFIRE SMOKE
8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1(b) defines the standard's central terms. "Current Air Quality Index (Current AQI)" is defined as "[t]he method used by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (U.S. EPA) to report air quality on a real-time basis," and the regulation notes that "[c]urrent AQI is also referred to as the “NowCast,” and represents data collected over time periods of varying length in order to reflect present conditions as accurately as possible." "PM2.5" is defined as "[s]olid particles and liquid droplets suspended in air, known as particulate matter, with an aerodynamic diameter of 2.5 micrometers or smaller." "Wildfire Smoke" is defined as "[e]missions from fires in “wildlands,” as defined in Title 8, section 3402, or in adjacent developed areas."

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "The method used by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (U.S. EPA) to report air quality on a real-time basis."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (b) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  "Current AQI is also referred to as the “NowCast,” and represents data collected over time periods of varying length in order to reflect present conditions as accurately as possible."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (b) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  "Solid particles and liquid droplets suspended in air, known as particulate matter, with an aerodynamic diameter of 2.5 micrometers or smaller."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (b) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  "Emissions from fires in “wildlands,” as defined in Title 8, section 3402, or in adjacent developed areas."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (b) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  Known gap: This clause does not restate the separate definition of "wildlands" found at 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3402, which the wildfire-smoke definition cross-references but which was not independently fetched or verified for this document.

EMPLOYER DUTY TO IDENTIFY PM2.5 EXPOSURE
8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1(c) requires that "[t]he employer shall determine employee exposure to PM2.5 for worksites covered by this section at the start of each shift and periodically thereafter, as needed to protect the health of employees, by any of the following methods." One listed method is to "[c]heck AQI forecasts and the current AQI for PM2.5 from any of the following websites: U.S. EPA AirNow, the Interagency Wildland Fire Air Quality Response Program, the U.S Forest Service, the California Air Resources Board, the local air pollution control district, or the local air quality management district." The regulation also allows an employer to obtain the same AQI information directly from those sources by telephone, email, or text, or to measure PM2.5 levels at the worksite directly and convert the reading to a corresponding AQI under Appendix A. An exception allows an employer to skip this determination step by assuming the current AQI for PM2.5 exceeds 500 and complying with the standard's requirements for that exposure level.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "The employer shall determine employee exposure to PM2.5 for worksites covered by this section at the start of each shift and periodically thereafter, as needed to protect the health of employees, by any of the following methods:"
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (c) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  "Check AQI forecasts and the current AQI for PM2.5 from any of the following websites: U.S. EPA AirNow, the Interagency Wildland Fire Air Quality Response Program, the U.S Forest Service, the California Air Resources Board, the local air pollution control district, or the local air quality management district"
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (c)(1) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  Known gap: This clause does not restate the technical PM2.5-to-AQI conversion methodology in Appendix A, which was not independently fetched or verified for this document.

HAZARD COMMUNICATION AND TRAINING REQUIREMENTS
8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1(d) requires that, as part of the employer's injury and illness prevention program under section 3203, "the employer shall establish and implement a system for communicating wildfire smoke hazards in a language and manner readily understandable by employees, including provisions designed to encourage employees to inform the employer of wildfire smoke hazards at the worksite without fear of reprisal." That system must inform employees of the current AQI for PM2.5 and of protective measures available to reduce their exposure, and must encourage employees to report worsening air quality or adverse symptoms such as asthma attacks, difficulty breathing, and chest pain. Separately, subsection (e) requires that, also under section 3203, "the employer shall provide employees with effective training and instruction in a language and manner readily understandable by employees," and that this training "shall contain the information in Appendix B" at a minimum.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "the employer shall establish and implement a system for communicating wildfire smoke hazards in a language and manner readily understandable by employees, including provisions designed to encourage employees to inform the employer of wildfire smoke hazards at the worksite without fear of reprisal."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (d) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  "the employer shall provide employees with effective training and instruction in a language and manner readily understandable by employees."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (e) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  "At a minimum, this shall contain the information in Appendix B."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (e) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  Known gap: This clause does not restate the specific content items listed in the regulation's Appendix B, which sets the minimum training curriculum but was not independently fetched or verified for this document.

ENGINEERING AND ADMINISTRATIVE CONTROL MEASURES
8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1(f)(1)-(2) sets a hierarchy of control measures once exposure at or above AQI 151 for PM2.5 is present. Engineering controls come first: "[t]he employer shall reduce employee exposure to PM2.5 to less than a current AQI of 151 by engineering controls whenever feasible, for instance by providing enclosed buildings, structures, or vehicles where the air is filtered," and "[i]f engineering controls are not sufficient to reduce exposure to PM2.5 to less than a current AQI of 151, then the employer shall reduce employee exposures to the extent feasible." Where engineering controls are not feasible or sufficient, administrative controls apply: "the employer shall implement administrative controls, if practicable, such as relocating work to a location where the current AQI for PM2.5 is lower, changing work schedules, reducing work intensity, or providing additional rest periods."

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "The employer shall reduce employee exposure to PM2.5 to less than a current AQI of 151 by engineering controls whenever feasible, for instance by providing enclosed buildings, structures, or vehicles where the air is filtered."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (f)(1) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  "If engineering controls are not sufficient to reduce exposure to PM2.5 to less than a current AQI of 151, then the employer shall reduce employee exposures to the extent feasible."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (f)(1) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  "the employer shall implement administrative controls, if practicable, such as relocating work to a location where the current AQI for PM2.5 is lower, changing work schedules, reducing work intensity, or providing additional rest periods."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (f)(2) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  Known gap: This clause does not evaluate whether any particular control measure is feasible or practicable at any specific worksite; the regulation itself leaves feasibility and practicability as case-by-case determinations.

RESPIRATOR REQUIREMENTS AT HIGHER AQI LEVELS
8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1(f)(3) sets two different respirator requirements depending on the severity of the current AQI for PM2.5. Between AQI 151 and 500, respirator use is voluntary but must be offered: "[w]here the current AQI for PM2.5 is equal to or greater than 151, but does not exceed 500, the employer shall provide a sufficient number of respirators to all employees for voluntary use in accordance with section 5144 and encourage employees to use respirators," and those "[r]espirators shall be NIOSH-approved devices that effectively protect the wearers from inhalation of PM2.5, such as N95 filtering facepiece respirators." Above AQI 500, respirator use becomes mandatory: "[w]here the current AQI for PM2.5 exceeds 500, respirator use is required," and "[r]espirators shall be used in accordance with section 5144."

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "Where the current AQI for PM2.5 is equal to or greater than 151, but does not exceed 500, the employer shall provide a sufficient number of respirators to all employees for voluntary use in accordance with section 5144 and encourage employees to use respirators."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (f)(3)(A) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  "Respirators shall be NIOSH-approved devices that effectively protect the wearers from inhalation of PM2.5, such as N95 filtering facepiece respirators."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (f)(3)(A) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  "Where the current AQI for PM2.5 exceeds 500, respirator use is required."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (f)(3)(B) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  Known gap: This clause does not restate the substantive fit-testing and medical-evaluation requirements of the separately cross-referenced respiratory protection standard, 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5144, which was not independently fetched or verified for this document (the regulation's own note states that fit testing and medical evaluations are not required for voluntary use of filtering facepieces such as N95 respirators).

EMERGENCY OPERATIONS EXCEPTION
8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1(f)(4) modifies the control-measure requirements for certain emergency work. It states that "[t]he following applies to emergency operations, including rescue and evacuation," and "also applies to utilities, communications, and medical operations that are directly aiding emergency operations or firefighting operations." For those operations, "[t]he employer shall comply with subsection (f)(3)(A) for all AQI levels equal to or greater than 151" — meaning voluntary-use respirators must be provided regardless of how high the AQI rises — while the engineering-control, administrative-control, and mandatory-respirator-above-500 requirements of subsections (f)(1), (f)(2), and (f)(3)(B) do not apply.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "The following applies to emergency operations, including rescue and evacuation."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (f)(4) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  "also applies to utilities, communications, and medical operations that are directly aiding emergency operations or firefighting operations."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (f)(4) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  "The employer shall comply with subsection (f)(3)(A) for all AQI levels equal to or greater than 151."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 5141.1, subd. (f)(4)(A) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5141_1.html)
  Known gap: This clause does not address how this emergency-operations exception interacts with other Cal/OSHA emergency-response standards outside section 5141.1 itself.

expectedJSON.body: 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1(f)(3) sets two different respirator requirements depending on the severity of the current AQI for PM2.5. Between AQI 151 and 500, respirator use is voluntary but must be offered: "[w]here the current AQI for PM2.5 is equal to or greater than 151, but does not exceed 500, the employer shall provide a sufficient number of respirators to all employees for voluntary use in accordance with section 5144 and encourage employees to use respirators," and those "[r]espirators shall be NIOSH-approved devices that effectively protect the wearers from inhalation of PM2.5, such as N95 filtering facepiece respirators." Above AQI 500, respirator use becomes mandatory: "[w]here the current AQI for PM2.5 exceeds 500, respirator use is required," and "[r]espirators shall be used in accordance with section 5144."

expectedJSON.body: 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 5141.1(f)(4) modifies the control-measure requirements for certain emergency work. It states that "[t]he following applies to emergency operations, including rescue and evacuation," and "also applies to utilities, communications, and medical operations that are directly aiding emergency operations or firefighting operations." For those operations, "[t]he employer shall comply with subsection (f)(3)(A) for all AQI levels equal to or greater than 151" — meaning voluntary-use respirators must be provided regardless of how high the AQI rises — while the engineering-control, administrative-control, and mandatory-respirator-above-500 requirements of subsections (f)(1), (f)(2), and (f)(3)(B) do not apply.
